cfg.val.sec.atrest_keychain: on — key derived from the secret in the OS keychain
cfg.val.sec.atrest_file: on — key derived from %s (no OS keychain here: whoever copies that file can open the stores; set CHATCLI_ENCRYPTION_KEY from a secret manager for stronger protection)
cfg.val.sec.atrest_off: off — CHATCLI_ENCRYPTION_KEY=off; new writes are plaintext, sealed files still open
cfg.val.sec.atrest_unavailable: unavailable — %s; new writes are plaintext and sealed files do not open until the key is reachable
cfg.val.sec.atrest_migration_done: yes — every store is sealed with the current key
cfg.val.sec.atrest_migration_partial: %d file(s) sealed, %d left for the next start (in use), %d error(s); /config security reseal retries
cfg.val.sec.atrest_migration_pending: pending — sealed on the next start, or now with /config security reseal
cfg.val.sec.atrest_covers_all: sessions and autosaves, transcripts, prompt history, park snapshots, long-term memory (stores, daily notes, summaries, vector index), knowledge contexts and their vectors, CCR archive, cost snapshots, attachments, memory exports, audit trail (per line)
sec.cmd.reseal_off: Encryption at rest is off (CHATCLI_ENCRYPTION_KEY=off, or no key is available); nothing to reseal.
sec.cmd.unseal_done: Encryption at rest is off: wrote %d of %d store file(s) back in plaintext (%d journal line(s)). An older version can read them now.
auth.keychain.key_missing: the credential key of this installation lives in the OS keychain (%s), which does not hold it or cannot be reached from here; not creating a new key, since it would orphan everything sealed with the real one. Unlock the keychain, or set CHATCLI_ENCRYPTION_KEY, or %s=file with the original key file restored
atrest.unavailable.warning: Encryption at rest is unavailable: %s. New data is written in plaintext and encrypted stores will not open until the key can be read (see /config security).
sec.cmd.suggest_recovery_key: Show the recovery key: keep it outside this machine to open your data anywhere
sec.cmd.recovery_env: Your stores are sealed with CHATCLI_ENCRYPTION_KEY: that value is your recovery key. Keep it in a password manager.
sec.cmd.recovery_not_tty: The recovery key is shown only in an interactive terminal.
sec.cmd.recovery_warning: Recovery key — anyone who has it can open your ChatCLI data. Keep it in a password manager, never in a file next to the data:
sec.cmd.recovery_howto: If the OS keychain is lost (reinstalled system, new machine), set %s to this value: every store sealed with the default key opens again. Run /config security reseal afterwards if you want to keep using it as your own key.
cfg.val.sec.atrest_recovery: the keychain holds the only copy; keep one outside this machine: /config security recovery-key
export.plaintext_notice: Note: your local stores are encrypted at rest, but this export is plaintext so it can be read and imported anywhere — keep it somewhere safe.
sec.cmd.suggest_use_keychain: Move every store from CHATCLI_ENCRYPTION_KEY to the OS keychain key
sec.cmd.use_keychain_not_env: Your stores already use the default key (or encryption is off): nothing to move.
sec.cmd.use_keychain_unavailable: The OS keychain key is not available here (%s); nothing was changed.
sec.cmd.use_keychain_done: Every store now uses the OS keychain key. Remove %s from your environment (.env, shell profile) — it is no longer needed.
sec.cmd.use_keychain_partial: Some stores were not moved (in use or unreadable). Keep the old key: remove %s, set it in %s, and run /config security reseal again.
